title: Protocol for the analysis of double-stranded RNAs in virus-infected insect cells using anti-dsRNA antibodies
protocol: Prepare the RNA electrophoresis apparatus for running.
Add the non-denaturing polyacrylamide solution into the cast.
Remove the polymerized polyacrylamide gel from the cast stand and then from the clamp assembly.
Rinse the glass plate surfaces with DEPEC-treated H2O to remove residual polyacrylamide gel.
Drain excess water.
Mount the gel in the upper chamber (2 gels for each cassette or 1 gel and an acrylic plate on the other side) with spacer plates outwards.
Place the upper chamber in the running electrophoresis tank.
Fill the upper chamber and the tank with 1× TBE running buffer.
Check for leaking from the chamber to the tank carefully.
Carefully remove the comb using clean powder-free gloves.
Rinse the wells with 1× TBE using a syringe to clean debris from lanes.
Calculate and transfer 5–10 μg of total RNA into pre-cooled 1.5 mL microtubes.
Add 6× DNA loading dye to RNA samples.
Quickly spin samples in a pre-cooled centrifuge and keep samples on ice.
Load lanes in the polyacrylamide gel(s) with RNA samples.
If any, load empty wells with equal volume of 6× DNA loading dye + nuclease-free H2O.
Run gel(s) for 30 min using a voltage of 50 V and then increase to 100 V.
Suit off the power supply when Xylene cyanole dye runs for 80%–90% of the gel.
Take thick blotting filter paper and cut them slightly larger than the membrane size.
Soak sponges and blotting filter paper in 0.5× TBE transfer buffer.
Remove short glass plate from gel cassette, then soak gel with spacer glass plate into transfer buffer.
Place a blotting filter paper on top of the gel after removing spacer glass plate.
Invert montage and remove spacer glass to place membrane setup.
Open transfer cassette and place soaked sponge followed by blotting filter paper with gel on black side.
Soak positively charged Nylon membrane in 0.5× TBE and place it on top of the gel, using roller to remove bubbles.
Place a small amount of transfer buffer and then a soaked blotting filter paper on top of the membrane.
Add a soaked sponge on top of the blotting filter paper.
Carefully close the transfer cassette.
Place the cassette in the transfer module with black side facing black side of module.
Fill the tank with transfer buffer and close lid.
Perform wet transfer for 30–60 min using a voltage of 35 V in a cold room (4°C–6°C).
Cut off power supply, open the transfer cassette, and take the membrane from the sandwich.
Cut off a piece of positively charged Nylon membrane with dimensions suitable for the number of samples and dilutions.
Prepare a RNA solution in nuclease-free H2O at a concentration of 0.5 μg/μL.
Create 10× dilutions of the RNA solution (6–8 points total).
Spot 4 μl of each sample onto pre-determined locations on the Nylon membrane.
Allow the spots to dry before proceeding with immunoblotting.
Place the RNA membrane into a container with 10 mL of PBS-Tween, with the RNA side facing up.
Prepare 10 mL of blocking solution (50 μg/mL Sheared Salmon DNA, 1× PBS-Tween, 5% non-fat milk wt:vol).
Remove PBS-Tween from the membrane and add 10 mL of the blocking solution.
Incubate the membrane overnight at 4°C in a rocking shaker.
Dilute anti-dsRNA antibodies in primary antibody solution (PBS-Tween, 2% non-fat dry milk wt:vol).
Remove blocking solution from the membrane and replace with 10 mL of primary antibody solution.
Incubate the membrane for 2 hours at room temperature in a rocking shaker.
Wash the membrane three times with 10 mL of PBS-Tween for 10 minutes at room temperature while rocking.
Prepare the secondary antibody dilution in PBS-Tween, 2% non-fat dry milk wt:vol.
Replace the PBS-Tween with 10 mL of the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature with agitation.
Remove secondary antibody solution.
Wash three times with 10 mL of PBS-Tween for 10 min at room temperature while rocking.
Cut a piece of plastic and lay onto the chemiluminescence detection tray.
Remove the RNA membrane from the PBS-Tween, drain excess liquid using a paper towel, and place the membrane on top of the plastic.
Add 250–500 μL of ECL substrate on top of the membrane and ensure homogeneous distribution throughout the membrane.
Incubate for 1 min and cover with another piece of plastic on top of the membrane to remove air bubbles.
Set the auto-exposure mode for detection of chemiluminescence on to the Fusion FX imager.
Test different exposure times to find the best image.
Carefully transfer the membrane back into the western blot incubation box.
Wash three times with 10 mL of PBS-Tween.
Dry the membrane on top of a paper towel with the RNA faced up at room temperature.
Count and transfer 10^7 cells into 15 mL conical tubes.
Infect S2 cells with 10^5 pfu of IIV-6 (0.01 pfu/cell) and 10^7 pfu of DCV (1 pfu/cell).
Incubate for 1 h at 25°C on a rotating shaker or manually rocking cells every 10 min.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Add fresh media to the cells and resuspend them at density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL with 10 mL serological pipettes.
Homogenize and transfer 2 mL of the cell suspension into each well in 6-well plates.
Incubate S2 cells at 25°C.
Add BrdU to homogenized S2 cells at a final concentration of 20 μM, 70 h post IIV-6 infection.
Incubate treated S2 cells for 1 hour at 25°C.
Soak coverslips in 100% ethanol for at least 5 seconds.
Transfer coverslips to sterilized double-distilled water (ddH2O) for 5 seconds.
Transfer coverslips back to 100% ethanol, then place them on the walls of an inverted 6-well plate lid to dry.
Soak single coverslip into wells in a 12-well plate with forceps.
Add 500 μL of Poly-L-lysine (0.01% wt:vol) or Concanavalin A (ConcA, 0.5 mg/mL) solution diluted in 1× PBS to each well of the 12-well plate.
Incubate within the hood for 1 hour.
Wash once with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Transfer infected S2 cells to poly-L-lysine- or Concanavalin A (ConcA)-treated coverslips at each indicated time point.
Resuspend cells into the media and homogenize.
Transfer 500 μL of the cell suspension into the wells of a 12-well plate containing coverslips.
Incubate cells for 1 hour at 25°C to allow cell attachment.
Remove the medium and fix cells with 4% formaldehyde solution (PFA) for 10–15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash three times with 1× PBS.
Incubate fixed cells for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 500 μL of PBSTX to each well, incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Repeat the permeabilization step once.
Remove PBSTX and add 500 μL of IFA blocking buffer into each well.
Incubate with IFA blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Prepare primary antibody solution in IFA blocking buffer.
On a Parafilm placed in the bottom of a 90 mm culture dish, add 25–50 μL of the anti-dsRNA solution for each sample (4–6 droplets/culture dish).
Take coverslips from the 12-well plate and place them face down on the anti-dsRNA droplet using a pipette tip and forceps.
Add cotton rolls imbibed in water to the culture dish without touching the Parafilm.
Cover the 90 mm culture dish with the lid and incubate overnight at 4°C.
Remove coverslips from the culture dish, transfer them into a 12-well plate containing PBSTX face up.
Wash coverslips three times with PBSTX for 5 min each.

Prepare secondary antibody solution in PBSTX (1:300 Goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 for detection of the monoclonal antibody J2, 1:300 Goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 546 for detection of 9D5 and 1:500 Hoechst for DNA staining).
Change the Parafilm in the 90 mm culture dish.
Add 25–50 μL droplets of the secondary antibody solution for each sample (4–6 droplets/culture dish).
Place the coverslips face down on the droplets.
Add cotton rolls imbibed with water to the culture dish, cover with a lid, and wrap in aluminum foil paper.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Remove coverslips from the culture dish, transfer them into wells of a 12-well plate (face up).
Wash three times with PBSTX for 5 minutes each.
Remove PBS and add 500 μL of 1× PBS to the wells containing coverslips.
Clean microscopy slides with 70%–100% ethanol using a lint-free wipe.
Add 10 μL of Hydromount medium onto microscope slides.
Carefully place the coverslip face down onto the Hydromount droplets.
Transfer the slides to a light-protective container and store at room temperature overnight.
Using transparent nail polish, seal the rim of the coverslips.
Transfer the slides to a light-protective container for nail polish drying (1–2 hours).
Store slides at 4°C until imaging.
For long storage, keep slides at −20°C.
Mount at least one coverslip for mock and another from infected cells in the same slide.
Select the proper objective lens and laser wavelengths to capture images.
Adjust the laser power, detector gain, resolution (number of pixels per image), single or stack acquisition, and file format to save images.
